messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: Traffic-shift stalled during cross-region failover. Controllers paused shift from eu-west -> ap-south after spike in TCP errors and SYN timeouts. Some customers reporting 5xx and long tail latencies. Pager routed to infra-oncall per escalation policy. See runbook infra/runbooks/traffic-shift-failures for immediate steps.

sam (oncall): Ack. I'm on call. Kicking off triage: check LB drain state, NAT/egress metrics, and DNS weight propagation. Pulling edge logs now.

kevin: Observed SYN retransmits and ECONNREFUSED from a subset of egress NAT gateways in ap-south. Also seeing BGP path changes from provider that briefly preferred an old route back to eu-west for a minority of prefixes. That mixed route + SNAT pool exhaustion explains asymmetric flows. Sample tcpdump from edge-ap-south-5:

```
12:03:21.123456 IP 10.40.50.60.52344 > 10.1.2.1.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
12:03:21.223999 IP 10.1.2.1.443 > 10.40.50.60.52344: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

kevin: NAT metrics: SNAT concurrent ports at ~98% on nat-gw-ap-south-1 for a 60s window. When ports exhausted, new outbound connections get immediate RSTs or get blackholed depending on provider behaviour.

anya: DNS control-plane kicked a 65% weight to ap-south earlier as part of the rollout. Some third-party resolver telemetry shows mixed answers; TTL was 30s. That combined with partial BGP path flips resulted in a subset of client flows attempting ap-south but egress SNAT not available, causing errors.

corey: Controller logic expects graceful drain: it waits for active session counts < threshold before moving to next step. Because sessions were unable to complete (many SYNs RSTing), active counts stayed high and controller paused the shift. It leaves the system in a half-failed state.

sam (oncall): Mitigation plan: (1) abort traffic-shift to roll back weights to stable baseline, (2) provision ephemeral extra SNAT capacity in ap-south and failover NATs, (3) force-drain problematic proxies and restart proxy daemon, (4) open provider ticket on BGP instability. Running dry-run abort then real abort if dry-run shows control-plane will revert.

incident-bot: ACTION: sam invoked traffic-shift abort --id=3302 --dry-run. Monitoring control-plane for 60s.

kevin: Provider status: cloud-network reports a degraded route reflector causing BGP flap between regions ~5-7m ago. They're investigating. Opening ticket: NET-APL-1223.

corey: While we wait, I'm applying a temporary routing policy that pins traffic for session-affine customers to current-region pools (no cross-region overflow) to reduce scope of impact. Applying to VIP group TopTier and Enterprise only.

sam (oncall): Dry-run shows control-plane will revert weights. I'm executing abort now. Also requesting ops automation to spin up two spare SNAT instances in ap-south and attach to NAT pool.

status-bot: ACTION: traffic-shift abort 3302 executed by sam. Rolling back region weights to previous stable config.

kevin: SNAT scale-up command run (cloud cli):

```
cloud nat create --region ap-south --type ephemeral --size medium --attach-pool nat-pool-ap-south-1
cloud nat attach --pool nat-pool-ap-south-1 --to vip-group api-prod
```

ops-bot: LOG: ephemeral SNAT instances provisioned and attached. Recomputing routing tables.

sam (oncall): Forcing cordon/drain + proxy restart on the nodes that show heavy SYN resets (edge-ap-south-5, edge-ap-south-8). Commands: 

```
kubectl cordon node/edge-ap-south-5
kubectl drain node/edge-ap-south-5 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/routing-proxy -n infra --field-selector spec.nodeName=edge-ap-south-5
```

kevin: After SNAT capacity increase and forced restarts, SYN error rates dropped to baseline. 5xx rate across the fleet went from 19% -> 1.8% within 7 minutes. Controller resumed normal state and did not attempt an automatic re-shift.

anya: DNS: control-plane rollback propagated. We still see a minority of resolvers with old ap-south answers — TTL window will clear in ~30s. Posting a note to status page that DNS may be inconsistent for up to TTL.

sam (oncall): Customer comms draft: "We detected failures during a regional traffic shift which caused intermittent errors for some customers. We rolled back the traffic shift, reprovisioned egress NAT capacity, and restarted affected proxies. Service recovery observed; continuing to monitor. We will follow up with a post-incident with timeline and root cause." Approve to publish?

corey: Approve. Send to affected accounts list (Enterprise: NovaPay, ResearchGrid) and status page.

incident-bot: UPDATE: mitigations applied. Monitoring 30m. Next scheduled update +15m. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Opening provider ticket NET-APL-1223 (BGP flap) and CLOUD-NAT-447 (SNAT port exhaustion behavior). Linking tcpdumps and SNAT metrics.

# Handoff

incident-bot: SCHEDULER: handoff to corey in 20m (per rotation).

corey: Taking over in 10. Outstanding: confirm provider response on BGP flap, ensure ephemeral SNAT stays healthy or convert to permanent capacity if needed, validate no residual 5xx spikes, and file post-incident doc. Runbook references: infra/runbooks/traffic-shift-failures and infra/runbooks/nat-troubleshooting.

sam (oncall): Summary for handoff: aborted shift 3302, provisioned ephemeral SNAT in ap-south, cordoned/drained edge-ap-south nodes and restarted routing proxy, temporary routing policy applied to limit cross-region overflow for top customers, customer notifications dispatched. Next steps: coordinate with networking to root cause BGP flaps, add pre-shift SNAT capacity check to rollout checklist, and add explicit controller breakpoint that validates egress path health before moving weights wide.

anya: Marking severity P1 because customer-facing errors occurred and multiple enterprise customers affected. Scheduling 1hr postmortem call in 90m. I'll draft initial timeline and link logs.

corey: I'll file the postincident ticket and schedule RCA. Assigning to eng-networking and eng-infra.

status-bot: LOG: notifications sent to NovaPay and ResearchGrid; support tickets created.

incident-bot: RESOLUTION: metrics stable for 25m. Incident moved to monitoring; postmortem pending. Closing active paging.

corey: Thanks all. I'll publish the incident doc and include recommended actions: pre-shift NAT capacity validation, BGP path monitoring integration, DNS fallback policy, and runbook updates for SNAT exhaustion.
